content: {"tool":"evaluate","args":{"name":"input_scale_2x","hypothesis":"Increasing sensitivity to horizontal velocity, body angle, and angular velocity by scaling them up will cause the policy to fire side thrusters earlier and correct attitude, reducing drift and improving landing safety under crosswind.","ops":[{"op":"input_affine","scale":[1.0,1.0,2.0,1.0,2.0,2.0,1.0,1.0]}]}}

feedback.name: input_scale_2x
feedback.hypothesis: Increasing sensitivity to horizontal velocity, body angle, and angular velocity by scaling them up will cause the policy to fire side thrusters earlier and correct attitude, reducing drift and improving landing safety under crosswind.

feedback.name: hv_scale2_side1.5
feedback.hypothesis: Increasing sensitivity to horizontal velocity (scale factor 2) will cause the policy to detect crosswind drift earlier, while boosting the logits for side‑thruster actions (scale factor 1.5 for actions 1 and 3) makes them more likely to be selected. This should lead to earlier and more decisive side‑engine firings, better attitude control, and higher safe‑landing rates under strong crosswind conditions.

feedback.name: attitude_scale2_main_offset
feedback.hypothesis: Scaling body angle and angular velocity (2×) makes the policy more sensitive to attitude errors, prompting earlier side‑engine corrections and stabilizing the lander under crosswind. Adding a small positive offset to the main‑engine logit (+0.2) encourages more main‑engine thrust for vertical braking, reducing crashes caused by insufficient deceleration.

feedback.name: hv_vv_scale1.5_side1.2_main_offset
feedback.hypothesis: Moderately scaling the horizontal and vertical velocity inputs (1.5×) makes the policy more responsive to drift and descent speed, while a modest 1.2× boost to the side‑engine logits and a small +0.1 offset to the main‑engine logit encourages earlier side‑thruster corrections and a bit more vertical braking. This should improve the safe‑landing rate under strong crosswind without destabilising the controller.

feedback.name: hv_scale2_side1.5_offset0.05
feedback.hypothesis: Doubling the horizontal velocity input makes the policy react earlier to crosswind drift, while a modest 1.5× boost to the side‑engine logits combined with a small +0.05 offset for both side‑engine actions encourages earlier side‑thruster firings without overshooting. This should reduce horizontal drift and improve the safe‑landing rate under strong crosswind.

feedback.name: height_hv_vv_scale2_side1.5_main_offset
feedback.hypothesis: Scaling height, horizontal velocity, and vertical velocity (2×, 2×, 1.5×) makes the policy more aware of altitude and drift, while boosting side‑engine logits (1.5×) and adding a small offset (+0.05) encourages earlier side‑thruster corrections. Adding a modest +0.1 offset to the main‑engine logit promotes more vertical braking. Together this should reduce cross‑wind drift and improve safe‑landing rates under strong crosswind.

feedback.name: x_hv_scale2_side1.5_offset0.2_main0.05
feedback.hypothesis: Doubling the horizontal position (x offset) and horizontal velocity inputs makes the policy more sensitive to lateral drift and off‑pad displacement, prompting earlier side‑engine corrections. A 1.5× boost to the side‑engine logits together with a +0.2 bias for both side‑engine actions encourages stronger side‑thruster firings, while a small +0.05 bias for the main‑engine action adds extra vertical braking. This combination should reduce cross‑wind drift and improve the safe‑landing rate under strong crosswind conditions.

feedback.name: reduce_side_thrusters_main_offset
feedback.hypothesis: Reducing side‑engine logits (scale 0.8) and applying a small negative bias (-0.05) discourages excessive side‑thruster firings that can cause overshoot, while adding a +0.2 offset to the main‑engine logit encourages stronger vertical braking. This should improve safe‑landing rates under crosswind by balancing horizontal correction and vertical deceleration.

feedback.name: reduce_side_thrusters_main_boost
feedback.hypothesis: Reducing side‑engine logits (0.8×) and applying a small negative bias (-0.05) curbs excessive horizontal corrections, while boosting the main‑engine logit (1.2×) and adding a +0.2 bias encourages stronger vertical braking. This balance should improve safe‑landing rates under strong crosswind by preventing side‑thruster overshoot and ensuring adequate descent control.

feedback.name: hv_height_scale1.5_reduce_side_main_boost
feedback.hypothesis: Scaling height and horizontal velocity (1.5×) makes the policy more aware of altitude and lateral drift, prompting earlier corrective actions. Reducing side‑engine logits (0.8×) with a small negative bias (-0.05) curbs excessive side‑thruster firings, while boosting the main‑engine logit (1.2×) and adding a +0.2 bias encourages stronger vertical braking. This balance should improve safe‑landing rates under strong crosswind without causing overshoot.

feedback.name: hv_height_vv_scale2_reduce_side_main_boost
feedback.hypothesis: Scaling height (2×), horizontal velocity (2×), and vertical velocity (1.5×) makes the policy more sensitive to altitude and drift, prompting earlier corrective actions. Reducing side‑engine logits (0.8×) with a small negative bias (-0.05) curbs excessive side‑thruster firings, while boosting the main‑engine logit (1.2×) and adding a +0.2 bias encourages stronger vertical braking. This balance should improve safe‑landing and solution rates under strong crosswind.

feedback.name: hv_height_vv_attitude_scale2_reduce_side_main_boost
feedback.hypothesis: Scaling height, horizontal velocity, vertical velocity, body angle, and angular velocity (2×, 2×, 1.5×, 2×, 2×) makes the policy more sensitive to altitude, drift, and attitude errors, prompting earlier corrective actions. Reducing side‑engine logits (0.8×) with a small negative bias (-0.05) curbs excessive side‑thruster firings, while boosting the main‑engine logit (1.2×) and adding a +0.2 bias encourages stronger vertical braking. This balance should improve both safe‑landing and solution rates under strong crosswind.
